text:
zoe: Starting rollout for release-2025.05.03 across api, runtime, console, router. Quiet window 00:30-02:30 UTC. Plan was 5% -> 20% -> 60%. Pin runtime to v3.3.0. Any immediate concerns?

deploy-bot: Dry-run OK. Command queued:

```
/deploy release-2025.05.03 --services api,runtime,console,router --canary 5,20,60 --pin runtime@v3.3.0 --observe 10m
```

mike: FYI router has new header-normalizer that drops unknown headers by default. We saw client 403s in canary last week. Recommend router start at 1% and enable tolerant-mode in canary.

zoe: agreed. Changing router canary to 1% and enabling router.header_tolerant=true for canary.

router-bot: Noted. Will set tolerant-mode for canary deployments.

deploy-bot: Wave 1 started at 5% (api,runtime,console,router@1%). Monitoring hooks attached.

ops-bot: Baseline: api_p95=130ms, error_rate=0.15%. Alert if error_rate>1% for 10m or p95>250ms for 10m.

tanya: seeing a rise in api 5xx at +7m, tracing points to router returning 403 for some UA strings. Count=18 in 6m.

mike: those UAs are old service bots; tolerant-mode should handle but maybe not for this header variant. Suggest pin router to 0% and continue api/runtime/console.

zoe: ok doing selective pin. Running:

```
/deploy pin traffic --service router --percent 0 --reason "header 403s on legacy UA"
/deploy continue release-2025.05.03 --services api,runtime,console --canary 5,20 --observe 10m
```

deploy-bot: Router pinned to 0%. Continuing other services.

ops-bot: Monitor kv_evictions and retry spikes. If kv_evictions>0.5% hold and scale.

tanya: api/runtime/console at 20% and stable after extended observe. No client errors.

mike: preparing minimal router patch (header parse fallback). ETA 40m. If patch fails, rollback router to v2.3.8.

zoe: adding to release notes: router held to 0% due to header-normalizer mismatch; non-router services completed canary. Runbook updated with rollback commands.

deploy-bot: Canary complete for api/runtime/console. Final rollout will wait on router patch. Thread left open for router follow-up. :white_check_mark:
